I'm the founder and CEO of Elevation Code Works, a software engineering business in Denver. I build and connect the software a small business's customers use, from the website that brings them in to the tools they use to book and pay.

I’ve spent 14 years building and modernizing software. Most recently I’ve been a lead software engineer at a large enterprise, building platforms used by millions of customers and leading AI adoption across engineering teams.

Earlier, I spent nearly five years as a contract engineer on federal projects, including work for the FDA, the Department of Veterans Affairs and the U.S. Census Bureau. That work taught me to build software that holds up under real scrutiny: secure, tested and maintainable long after launch.

I’ve trained hundreds of enterprise engineers on AI-assisted and spec-driven development, and I work the same way for every client. Before I build anything, I write down what the software must do and you approve it. AI speeds up the work, and I stay accountable for every decision and every result.
B.S. in Computer Science, University of Maryland

text: Practical AI built into your website or app, such as assistants that answer customer questions from your own information, smarter intake forms and help with booking.

AI is useful when it does a specific job well and someone stays responsible for it. I build features that answer your customers’ real questions from your own information, with limits you set and review.

I also use AI to build faster. I’ve trained hundreds of enterprise engineers on AI-assisted development, and I use the same practices on every project. AI speeds up the work. I make the decisions and I’m accountable for the result.
Businesses that answer the same customer questions every day, or lose people during intake and booking.
A website assistant that answers questions from your own content and hands the conversation to you when it should.
Intake forms that ask useful follow-up questions and summarize each request for you.
Help for customers choosing a service or a time to book.
Clear limits on what the AI may say, what it must not, and how you review it.

text: Ongoing care for your website and customer-facing apps, and help when a project has stalled or a developer has disappeared.
A website is never finished. Software it depends on goes out of date, security fixes pile up, and a small problem can quietly cost you customers for months.

I look after sites and customer-facing apps on a regular schedule, and I take over projects that have stalled. I start with an honest review of what’s there, then fix what matters first. When something old needs replacing, I modernize it in steps so the business keeps running.
Businesses with a site or app that nobody is looking after, or one that is slow, broken or built on software that is out of date.
Updates, security patches, backups and uptime checks on a regular schedule.
Taking over an existing project, starting with an honest review of what's there and a plan.
Modernizing an old site or app one piece at a time, without a risky rewrite.
Care for back-office systems such as accounting or inventory software.
Office IT support for computers, printers and networks.

Connect payments, online stores and booking tools to your website or app, so customers can pay and book in one place.
Most small businesses already pay for good tools. The trouble starts when those tools don’t talk to the website, and customers get bounced between pages that look and work differently.

I connect the payment, store and booking tools you use into your site or app, so a customer can find you, book and pay without leaving. When a ready-made integration exists I use it. When it doesn’t, I build a small, documented connection that you own.
Businesses that take payments, sell online or book appointments, and want those tools to work with their website instead of beside it.
Payments with Stripe or Square, including checkout, invoices, subscriptions and memberships.
Online stores on Shopify, including connecting a store to an existing website.
Booking and scheduling tools, set up so customers can book from your site and receive confirmations and reminders.
Small custom connections and webhooks where no ready-made integration exists.

text: Fast, accessible websites built so search engines can read every page and customers can find you and get in touch.
Most small business websites have the same problems: they load slowly on phones, search engines can’t tell what the business does, and nobody remembers how to update them.

I build sites that fix all three. Every page loads quickly, carries the information search engines look for, and works for every visitor. Rankings also depend on things outside the website, like reviews and your Google Business Profile. I’ll tell you what matters there, but I don’t run marketing campaigns.
Small businesses whose website is slow, dated, hard to update, or missing from search results.
A custom site built for phones first and tuned to pass Google's Core Web Vitals.
Search-ready structure on every page, including titles, descriptions, a sitemap and structured data that tells Google what your business is and where it works.
Accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA, so the site works for every visitor, including people using a keyboard or screen reader.
Hosting set up in your own accounts, so you own the site and its domain.
A handoff covering how to make the updates you'll need most often.
Ongoing SEO campaigns, link building or content marketing.
Paid ads or social media management.
Managing your Google Business Profile or reviews.

Skiers, riders and anyone planning a day outdoors who wants a fast read on the weather.

Condies answers one question quickly: when are conditions best? It shows the current weather, the next twelve hours, and a week of temperature ranges, then picks the best day and time to head out and scores it out of 100.
Saved spots and a map, so regular destinations are one tap away.

Skiers and splitboarders who climb resorts before the lifts open or after they close.

Uphill rules change every season and are scattered across 24 resort websites. Uphill Ski CO puts them in one place: hours, costs and routes, ranked from most to least accessible, with each resort’s status marked as confirmed for this season or carried over from the last.
Search by name and filter by pass network or by whether uphill travel is allowed while lifts run.

Frontend work for Important, Not Important, plus backend and dev-ops improvements that made the app faster and more secure.

What Can I Do? helps people find concrete ways to act on the issues they care about. Visitors search by location and get actions they can take right away: places to donate or volunteer, things to learn, and products to buy from proven solutions.

Important, Not Important brought me in to take on frontend tasks on the What Can I Do? app. Along the way, I suggested and built a few backend and dev-ops improvements that made it faster and more secure.

We needed help implementing some frontend tasks on our app and Tejen was able to seamlessly step in and get them done. Not only that, he suggested and implemented a few backend and dev-ops features that made the app faster and more secure. His intuition and knowledge of modern web development make him an easy recommendation.
